subject: Framework version changed to a different standard - blocking audit prep
body:
Hi,

When I logged in today I noticed our framework has switched to a different version of the standard than what we've been working from - the control numbers and requirements don't match what our team has been mapping evidence to for the past several months.

Can someone tell me why this happened and how to get it back to the version we were originally set up on? We have an audit starting very soon and this has completely stopped our prep - none of our existing evidence mappings line up with the new numbering, so we can't tell what's still covered and what isn't.

This is blocking us entirely right now, there's no way for us to work around it on our end. Please let me know what's going on and how quickly this can be sorted out.

Thanks

subject: Can I run two frameworks at once? (need a straight answer before I add ISO 27001)
body:
We're currently set up on SOC 2 and now need to add ISO 27001 since we have an audit coming up later this year. Before I go add the second framework in the platform, I need to know if this is actually supported or if it's going to break something / duplicate a bunch of work.

I've looked through the app and can't find anything that tells me one way or the other whether running two frameworks at the same time is fine, or if it causes issues with evidence collection duplicating across shared controls. This should honestly just be stated somewhere in the UI before you add a framework - I don't want to click "add" and then find out three weeks from now that half our evidence got collected twice or mapped wrong, that's going to make us look completely unprepared to the auditor.

Right now I'm just manually cross-checking our SOC 2 controls against the ISO 27001 control list in a spreadsheet before adding anything, which is slow and defeats the point of using this tool in the first place. Can someone confirm definitively whether it's safe to add a second framework without creating duplicate evidence requests, and if so why isn't this communicated anywhere when you go to add one? This is exactly the kind of thing that should be obvious up front, not something we have to open a ticket to find out.

subject: URGENT: Readiness score stuck at 0% - need this fixed ASAP
body:
Hi,

We need help on this right away, it's blocking our work. I manually added a batch of controls last week and marked every single one of them as "Complete" - I've triple checked and they all show the Complete status. But the overall readiness score on our dashboard is stuck at 0% and it's not moving at all, even after waiting for it to refresh overnight.

This makes no sense to me - if controls are complete, the score should reflect that. Can you please add a way to force a recalculation of the readiness score, or at least make it update automatically when controls are added manually? Right now there's no way for us to get an accurate percentage and we're stuck until this is resolved.

Please treat this as urgent, we need a fix or a workaround fast.

Thanks

subject: Duplicate controls across frameworks + reconsidering our plan
body:
We have two frameworks active in our account, and what should clearly be the same control is showing up as two completely separate controls instead of being mapped/shared between them. I've gone in and manually cross-referenced them to confirm they're supposed to be the same requirement, but the platform just isn't linking them like I'd expect. I can obviously duplicate my evidence uploads by hand across both, but that's exactly the kind of manual busywork we bought this tool to get away from.

Honestly this is making me question what we're paying for. When we signed up, the pitch was that overlapping requirements across frameworks would be handled for us, not something we have to reconcile ourselves every time. I don't want to have to loop in my leadership to explain why we're paying for a "compliance automation" platform when a good chunk of the work is still manual, but that conversation is starting to feel unavoidable if this doesn't get sorted.

Separately, and maybe related to the same underlying issue, I'm also finding it hard to get a clear picture of how we're actually implementing and tracking controls over time. It's not obvious where to see status/progress in a way that's useful for reporting internally, so any guidance there would help too.

I'd really like to understand why this is happening and what can be done, because right now it feels like we're paying for automation and doing manual reconciliation work anyway. Please let me know how this can be fixed or explained, because otherwise we're going to have to seriously look at whether this is the right tool for us.

subject: Can I run two frameworks at the same time?
body:
We're currently set up on SOC 2 and now need to add ISO 27001 as well since we have an audit coming up later this year. Before I go and add the second framework, I need to know - can this platform actually handle two frameworks running at once, or is it going to duplicate all my evidence collection and controls work?

I looked through the app and couldn't find anything that explains what happens when you add a second framework on top of an existing one. Does it merge shared controls automatically, or am I going to end up manually uploading the same evidence twice for overlapping controls? I really don't want to find out the hard way after I've already added it and made a mess of our control mapping.

This is honestly pretty frustrating - I've spent time digging through docs and support articles and can't find a clear answer, and I don't want to waste more time guessing or have to manually cross-reference everything between two frameworks if the tool doesn't handle it natively. Can someone just tell me plainly whether this is supported and what actually happens to shared controls/evidence when you do it? Thanks.

subject: Wrong company name on invoices - need a way to fix this ourselves
body:
Our invoices are showing the wrong legal company name and I cannot find anywhere in the billing or account settings to correct it. I've gone through every settings page I can find and there's just no option to update this ourselves - it seems like something only support can touch on the backend, which honestly isn't good enough for a paid platform.

This is actually the same issue causing the name mismatch we've now noticed on our issued framework certificate too - the certificate has the wrong entity name printed on it, which is a real problem for us since that's a document we share externally with clients and partners. Having our correct legal name on file should be basic account hygiene, and the fact that there's no self-serve way to fix it once it's wrong is a serious gap.

We can go in and manually edit our copies of the invoices for now as a workaround, but that's not sustainable long term and doesn't fix the certificate issue at all. I'd like to formally request that you add an editable company/legal entity name field somewhere in account settings so we can manage this ourselves going forward.

Honestly, this is becoming a bigger issue than it should be. We're now having internal conversations about whether this platform can actually support how our business operates, and I've been asked to raise this with our leadership as a point of concern. I'd really appreciate if someone could look into both a fix for our current documents and a real product fix so this doesn't keep happening.

subject: Request credit/discount - already completed scoping work for ISO 27001 elsewhere
body:
Hi,

We already went through the full scoping process for ISO 27001 outside of your platform before we signed up, and now we're being asked to redo essentially the same scoping work again from scratch for SOC 2 inside the platform. This is a duplicate of work we've already paid for and completed elsewhere, so we don't think we should have to pay full price or spend the time redoing it.

Can you either credit our account for this or adjust our billing to reflect that we shouldn't have to redo scoping we've already done? We have an auditor scheduled to start very soon and this is currently blocking us from moving forward, so we need this resolved quickly. There's no way for us to work around it on our end right now.

Please let me know what you can do.

Thanks

subject: Bug: Can't view GDPR controls without committing to add the framework
body:
This is honestly becoming a dealbreaker for us. We're trying to evaluate the GDPR control set before deciding whether to actually add it to our account, but there's no way to just look at what's included. The only option is to add the framework outright - there's no preview, no read-only view, nothing.

That seems like a bug to me. Every other part of the platform lets you look before you commit, so why would this one force us to add a whole framework to our account just to see what controls come with it? We shouldn't have to fully provision something we're not even sure we want yet.

Right now the only workaround is to manually dig through GDPR requirements ourselves outside the platform and cross-reference against what we think your control set covers, which defeats the purpose of paying for a compliance tool in the first place. It's slow and honestly makes me question what else in here is going to require this kind of workaround.

We're actively discussing whether this platform is even the right fit anymore, and issues like this aren't helping. Can someone please look into this and fix it so we can preview a framework's controls before adding it? I'd like to get this resolved before we make any decisions about renewing.

subject: Feature request: import/reuse existing ISO 27001 scoping for SOC 2
body:
Hi,

We already completed all the scoping work for ISO 27001 outside of your platform (systems, boundaries, in-scope processes, etc.) before we started using this tool. Now that we're setting up SOC 2 in the platform, it's asking us to go through the entire scoping process again from scratch as if none of that work exists.

Since the scoping is largely equivalent between the two frameworks, we don't want to redo all of it manually inside the platform - it's a lot of duplicate effort for work we've already done. Is there a way to import or map our existing scoping so it carries over to the new SOC 2 framework setup instead of starting over?

Right now there's no way for us to move forward without repeating all of that work, and we have our SOC 2 audit coming up very soon, so this is holding up our prep. Can you let us know if this is something that can be added, or if there's a way to handle this that we're missing?

Thanks,

subject: Wrong company name on our certificate - need this fixed, billing account issue?
body:
Hi,

We just noticed that the company name printed on our framework certificate does not match our actual legal entity name. This is a pretty big problem for us since we hand this certificate to clients and partners, and it makes us look sloppy when the name doesn't even match our official paperwork.

I've gone through account settings and the certificate section but there is no option anywhere to correct the company name ourselves. Is this tied to how the account/billing profile was originally set up? If so, can someone on your end update the legal entity name so it's reflected correctly on the certificate?

We do have an audit coming up in a few months, so I'd like to get this sorted well before then, but honestly this should have been right from the start and now I have to spend time chasing it down instead of doing actual work. If there's a manual way to get it corrected in the meantime please point me to it, but I'd really like a permanent fix so we're not dealing with this again on the next renewal.

Please advise ASAP.

Thanks,

subject: URGENT - Readiness score says 100% but auditor is finding gaps - need answers ASAP
body:
This needs to be looked at immediately, we are completely stuck right now.

Our dashboard has been showing 100% readiness for our framework for weeks. We trusted that number and told our team we were fully prepared. Now our auditor is going through fieldwork and is flagging actual gaps in controls that your platform shows as fully complete and green across the board.

How is this possible if we are at 100%? This is a serious problem because it means the readiness score is not reflecting reality, and we have no way of knowing what else might be wrong. We can't move forward with confidence until we understand why the platform told us everything was fine when it clearly wasn't.

I need someone to explain what is going on and how to fix this urgently - we are blocked and cannot proceed until this is resolved. Please treat this as high priority, this is impacting us right now and we don't have a workaround.

Please get back to me as soon as possible.

subject: Is there any way to preview the GDPR control set before adding the framework?
body:
We're trying to decide whether to add the GDPR framework to our account, but it looks like the only way to actually see the controls included in that set is to add the framework first and commit to it. That doesn't work for us - we need to know what we're actually getting (which controls, how they map to what we already have set up, overlap with our existing frameworks, etc.) before we turn it on.

Is there a preview option somewhere that I'm just not finding, or is this genuinely not possible right now? I know I could probably ask our rep or dig through documentation to piece together a manual list of what's in the GDPR set, but that's a pretty slow and unreliable way to evaluate whether this is worth adding.

Honestly this is becoming a real sticking point for us. We're currently comparing your platform against a couple other compliance tools, and not being able to preview a framework before committing to it is a pretty basic gap. If there's no way to do this, I'd like to understand why, because right now it's making me question whether we're going to stick with this platform. Please let me know either way - I'd rather get an answer than keep guessing.

subject: Scoping work from ISO 27001 not carrying over to SOC 2 - blocking audit prep
body:
We already completed the full scoping process for ISO 27001 (outside of your platform, before we onboarded) and now need to set up SOC 2 in the platform as well. When I go to start the SOC 2 scoping section, it's asking us to go through everything from scratch - defining boundaries, systems, in-scope processes, etc. - as if none of that work exists.

This doesn't make sense since we already did the equivalent scoping for ISO 27001 and the two frameworks overlap significantly. There should be some way for that work to carry over or at least be referenced so we're not duplicating effort.

Right now there's no way for us to move forward without redoing all of it manually, and our SOC 2 audit is coming up very soon so this is holding up our prep. We need this resolved as quickly as possible since we can't proceed with the audit until scoping is finalized in the system.

Can you look into why this isn't linking up and get us a way to move past it?

subject: Company name on certificate doesn't match our legal entity name - no way to fix it myself
body:
We just noticed that the company name printed on our framework certificate doesn't match our actual legal entity name. This is embarrassing, we already sent this out to a partner as proof of compliance and now have to go back and explain the discrepancy.

I've gone through account settings, org settings, everything I can think of, and there's no option anywhere to correct the legal entity name so it reflects properly on the certificate. It seems like this has to be fixed on your end, but there's no obvious way to request that either - I ended up having to just recreate a corrected version by hand as a stopgap, which isn't ideal since it's not the actual certificate your system generates.

Can you please add a way for us to edit/correct the legal entity name ourselves so it's reflected accurately on any certificates we generate going forward? This shouldn't require a support ticket every time. We have an audit coming up down the line and I don't want to be dealing with this same issue again when that rolls around.

Please let me know if there's a fix in the meantime for our current certificate as well.

subject: URGENT - Need to know which controls are automated vs manual
body:
Hi,

I need a fast answer on this because it's blocking me from moving forward - can someone please explain the actual difference between "automated" and "manual" controls in the platform? I'm going through my assigned controls list and I can't tell which ones are being tested automatically vs which ones I need to upload evidence for myself. There's nothing on the control page itself that tells me which type it is.

This is holding me up because I don't know if I should be uploading evidence right now or just waiting for a sync to run. I don't want to waste time uploading stuff that isn't needed, or worse, miss something that actually requires manual evidence from me.

Can you either tell me quickly how to identify this for each control, or better yet, please add a label/indicator directly on the control page so this is clear going forward? This shouldn't require guessing or contacting support every time.

Please get back to me as soon as possible - I'm stuck until I know how to proceed.

Thanks

subject: Can I mark a control as not applicable? Need an answer before we decide on renewal
body:
Hi,

We need to know if it's even possible to mark a control as "not applicable" so it stops dragging down our readiness score for controls that genuinely don't apply to our setup. I've looked through the controls list and can't find any option to do this anywhere.

Honestly this is starting to be a real problem for us. We're paying for this platform to make compliance easier, not to have our score penalized for things that flat out don't apply to our business. If there's no way to exclude irrelevant controls, we're going to have to seriously reconsider whether this tool is worth what we're paying for it, and I'll need to bring this up with my leadership team as part of that conversation.

Can someone confirm one way or the other whether this is possible, and if so, how? If it's not possible, I need to know that too so we can decide how to move forward.

Thanks,
Frustrated customer

subject: Can't tell if a control is automated or manual - blocking audit prep
body:
Our auditor is starting their review any day now and I'm going through our controls to make sure everything is up to date, but I can't figure out on the control page itself whether a given control is supposed to be tested automatically (via some integration sync I'm assuming) or if I'm actually supposed to be uploading evidence for it manually.

There's nothing on the control page that says which type it is. So for a bunch of controls I genuinely don't know if I should be doing anything at all or if I'm just waiting on it to sync on its own. This is a real problem because if I skip something that actually needed manual evidence, we're going to walk into the audit with gaps.

Can you explain the difference between automated and manual controls, and more importantly, can this be fixed so it's clearly labeled on each control's page? I don't have a way to work around this right now - I need to know control by control what's expected before I can finish getting ready. Please treat this as urgent, we're on a tight timeline.

subject: Can I mark a control as not applicable?
body:
We have a handful of controls in our readiness score that just don't apply to us (things like physical data center controls since we're fully cloud-hosted). I've been clicking around the controls list for a while now trying to find a way to exclude them or mark them as not applicable, but I can't find anything.

Right now these controls are dragging our readiness score down for no real reason, and honestly it's making it look like we're less prepared than we actually are. We have an audit coming up later this year and I'd rather not walk in with a score that looks worse than reality because of controls that don't even apply to our setup.

Is there an actual way to mark a control as not applicable, or do we just have to manually track which ones to ignore on our end? If there's a workaround I can use for now that's fine, but this has already cost me time I didn't need to spend, and I'd like a straight answer on whether this is even possible in the platform.

subject: URGENT - Bug: Can't tell if my controls are automated or manual, blocking me from completing anything
body:
This is urgent, I need help ASAP.

I'm going through my assigned controls right now and I have no idea which ones are supposed to be tested automatically vs which ones I need to manually upload evidence for. The control pages don't say anything about this - there's no label, no indicator, nothing that tells me what type of control I'm looking at.

I've clicked into probably 10 different controls trying to find where this is shown and it's just not there. Am I supposed to guess? I don't want to waste time uploading evidence for something that's already being handled automatically, but I also don't want to leave something unfinished thinking it's automated when it's not.

There's no way for me to work around this - I literally cannot proceed with my controls until I know which category each one falls into. Can someone please fix this or at least tell me where I'm supposed to be seeing this information? I need this resolved quickly, this is blocking my whole workflow right now.

Thanks.

subject: Need to mark controls as Not Applicable - and question about connecting cloud accounts
body:
Hi,

I've been going through our controls list trying to figure out how to exclude the ones that just don't apply to us (we're a small team and a handful of these controls are for things we don't even do), and I can't find any way to mark a control as Not Applicable anywhere on the controls list. Right now they're all just dragging down our readiness score for no reason, which makes our compliance posture look worse than it actually is.

Is this even possible in the platform? If not, this really needs to be a feature - we're evaluating other tools right now partly because of this, and if we can't get an accurate score that reflects our actual scope, it's hard to justify sticking with this platform. I know I could probably just document these exclusions manually somewhere and explain it to whoever reviews things, but that's not a real solution when the whole point of paying for this tool is to have accurate automated scoring.

Separate issue while I have you - I've also been trying to figure out how to connect our cloud/SaaS accounts (AWS and Google Workspace) so evidence collection happens automatically instead of us uploading screenshots by hand every time. I don't see a clear way to set that up either. Between these two things it's starting to feel like we're doing more manual work than the automation is supposed to save us, which is frustrating given what we're paying for this.

Can someone help with both of these, or at least tell me if they're on a roadmap? At this point I need to know whether this platform can actually do what we need or if we should be looking elsewhere.

Thanks,
A frustrated admin

subject: Need bulk update option for control statuses - billing/upgrade question
body:
Hi,

After our last internal review I had to go through and update the status on close to 80 controls, and there's no way to do that except clicking into each control one at a time. That took an entire afternoon by itself, and I don't see any option to select multiple controls and change their status together.

Our audit is starting very soon and I need to get all our control statuses current before then. Since there's no way around this on my end, can you tell me if bulk status updates are available on a higher plan tier, or if this is something that could be added to our account? I'd rather pay for the right plan/feature than keep doing this one by one, especially with the timeline we're on.

Please let me know what options I have and how quickly this could be turned on if it requires an upgrade.

Thanks

subject: No notification when reassigning control ownership
body:
I reassigned ownership of a control to a teammate last week and just found out today, completely by accident, that she had no idea it had been assigned to her. I only found out because I mentioned it to her in passing - she never got any kind of alert, email, or in-app notification that she was now responsible for it.

This is a real problem. We have an audit coming up later this year and controls sitting untouched because the new owner doesn't even know they own them is not a great look. I basically have to manually message every person every time I reassign something now to make sure they actually see it, which defeats the purpose of having this tracked in the platform in the first place.

Is there really no notification system for control reassignment? If not, this needs to be added ASAP because right now the only way to make sure someone knows they own a control is to tell them yourself, which is slow and easy to forget, and it's already made me look disorganized in front of my team. Please let me know if I'm missing a setting somewhere, otherwise please treat this as a bug/missing feature that needs fixing.

subject: URGENT: Shared control edit only applied to one framework, not both
body:
Hi,

I need help with this ASAP - we have a control that's mapped to both of our frameworks (ISO 27001 and SOC 2), and I edited the description on it earlier today. When I went to check, the updated description only shows up under one of the frameworks. The other framework still has the old, outdated description on what's supposed to be the same shared control.

I thought editing a shared control was supposed to update it everywhere it's mapped, not just wherever I happened to be looking at it when I made the change. Is this a bug? I can't find any setting or option to sync the two copies, and I don't want to have to manually track down and edit every instance every time something changes - that defeats the whole point of it being "shared."

This is urgent because we're actively updating control language and need both frameworks to reflect the correct, current descriptions right now. There's no workaround I can find, so I'm stuck until this is sorted out. Can someone please look into this quickly and let me know what's going on?

Thanks,
[Customer]

subject: Bug: Controls showing "Passed" even when automated test hasn't run in weeks
body:
This is a pretty serious gap and honestly it's making me question whether this platform can be trusted for what we're using it for.

We have controls that rely on automated tests, and right now if the test hasn't actually run in over 30 days, the control still just sits there showing "Passed" based on the last result it happened to get. There is no way to configure it to auto-fail or flag a control when the underlying test has gone stale. So a control can look green and healthy in the dashboard while the test behind it hasn't executed in a month or more. That's not a status I can rely on - it's just an old result being carried forward indefinitely.

I've gone through the settings for each control and there is nothing that lets me set a "must have run within X days or fail" rule. I even tried digging into notification/alerting settings thinking maybe it was buried there, but nothing.

Right now the only way I can catch this is to manually check the last-run timestamp on every single control myself on a regular basis, which defeats the entire point of having automated compliance monitoring. If I'm going to be manually auditing my automated tests anyway, I don't know why we're paying for this.

Can someone confirm whether this is being looked at as a bug, or tell me if there's a setting I'm somehow missing? If this isn't something that's getting fixed, we're going to need to seriously reconsider whether this platform is the right fit for us going forward. I'd like a real answer, not just a workaround suggestion.

subject: Need version history on control notes field
body:
Hi,

We just noticed that the notes field on a control only shows the most recent text that was entered - once someone edits it, whatever was written before is gone. We have a couple of controls where a teammate had written notes with important context and then someone else edited the field afterward, and now that original text is nowhere to be found.

Can you add some kind of version history or audit trail for the notes field so we can see who wrote what and when, and recover earlier versions if needed? Right now there's no way for us to get that information back once it's overwritten.

This is a real problem for us right now because we have an audit coming up very soon and we need to be able to show the history of what was documented on these controls, not just the latest edit. We're stuck on this - there's no way for us to work around it on our end, so we'd really appreciate a fix or at least a way to recover the missing notes as soon as possible.

Thanks.

subject: Missing evidence guidance on custom controls - billing question
body:
Hi,

I need to flag something that's cost us real time and I want to understand what we're actually paying for here.

We wrote several custom controls ourselves for parts of our program that aren't covered by the templates, and none of them show any indication of what evidence would actually satisfy them. When I open one of the template controls, there's a clear description of the kind of evidence expected. Our custom ones just... don't have that. Nothing. So my team has been guessing at what to upload, going back and forth internally, and honestly it's made us look disorganized when we've had to explain to our own stakeholders why we're not sure if what we've collected is even the right evidence.

We've been working around it by manually figuring out and documenting evidence requirements ourselves for each custom control, but that's slow and defeats the purpose of paying for a platform that's supposed to guide us through this. We do have an audit coming up down the road, so this isn't something we can just leave broken indefinitely.

Given that this is a core part of what we're paying for (the platform is supposed to tell you what evidence satisfies a control, template or not), I'd like to know:

1. Is this expected behavior for self-authored controls, or is something misconfigured on our account?
2. If this is just how custom controls work, why are we being charged the same as if we had full guidance across all our controls? Feels like we're paying for a feature we don't fully have access to.
3. Can we get a credit or adjustment for the time this has cost us, or get this fixed so custom controls get the same evidence guidance as templates?

Please let me know how you want to handle this. Thanks.

subject: URGENT: Need to assign TWO owners to a single control - currently impossible
body:
This is urgent and is currently blocking us.

We have several controls that are jointly owned by two people on our team - it's not a case of one person being "primary" and the other backup, they genuinely share the responsibility day to day. When I try to set this up in the platform, the control only lets me assign ONE owner. There's no field, dropdown, or option anywhere to add a second person as an owner on the same control.

This is a real problem for us - assigning it to just one of them misrepresents who's actually accountable, and we can't just pick one person to "own" it when that's not how our team actually works. I've looked everywhere in the control settings and can't find any way around this.

Please fix this ASAP or tell me if there's some setting I'm missing, because right now we're completely stuck and can't accurately reflect ownership on these controls. Need a fast response on this one.

subject: Bug: Cannot update multiple controls at once - massive waste of time
body:
This has to be a bug, or at least a huge oversight - there's no way to select multiple controls and update their status in one go. I have to click into every single control one at a time to change the status, and when you're dealing with dozens of controls after a review, that turns into an entire afternoon of pointless clicking.

I just went through this and lost hours doing something that should take minutes. If this is really how the platform is designed, that's honestly hard to believe - every other tool we use has basic bulk actions like select-all and apply status change. This feels like such a basic piece of functionality to be missing.

I'm going to be honest, this is the kind of thing that's making us seriously reconsider whether this platform is worth what we're paying for it. I need someone to tell me either this is a known bug that's getting fixed soon, or that there's a bulk update option I'm somehow not seeing. If neither of those is true, I'll need to escalate this internally because it's not sustainable for our team to keep doing this one control at a time.

Please advise ASAP.

subject: No notification when control ownership is reassigned
body:
I reassigned one of our controls to a teammate earlier this week, and they had absolutely no idea it happened until I mentioned it to them directly. There was no email, no in-app alert, nothing - they only found out because I brought it up in passing.

This seems like a bug since the whole point of reassigning ownership is so the new owner knows they need to act on it. Right now nothing tells them.

We're in the middle of prepping for our audit and controls are actively being reviewed and updated, so this is a real problem - people are missing owner responsibilities because they don't even know something was assigned to them. I don't see any way to work around this on my end (no setting to turn on notifications that I could find), so we're stuck relying on manually telling every teammate any time we reassign something, which isn't sustainable with everything else going on right now.

Can you confirm whether this is expected behavior or a bug, and if it's a bug, how soon it can be fixed? We need owners to actually be notified when a control is reassigned to them.

subject: Shared control edits don't sync across frameworks - need this fixed
body:
Hi,

I mapped a control across both our SOC 2 and ISO 27001 frameworks since it's the same control, and last week I updated the description on it to reflect a process change. I just noticed today that the update only shows up under SOC 2 - the ISO 27001 copy still has the old description.

This is really frustrating because I assumed editing a shared control would update it everywhere, that's the whole point of mapping it across frameworks in the first place. Now I have no idea how many other shared controls are out of sync because I edited them while only looking at one framework. I have to go through and manually check/update every shared control in both frameworks to make sure they match, which is a huge time sink.

We have an audit coming up later this year and the last thing I need is an auditor pulling up a control and seeing two different descriptions for what's supposed to be the same control. That makes us look like we don't have our documentation under control, which is exactly the opposite of what this tool is supposed to help with.

Can you please make it so that editing a shared control updates it consistently across every framework it's mapped to, regardless of which one you're viewing when you make the edit? This seems like pretty basic functionality for a tool that's supposed to handle cross-framework mapping.

Thanks,
A frustrated but hopeful customer

subject: Evidence showing as expired right after upload
body:

We're unable to log into the platform via SSO. When we try to sign in, it just bounces back and forth between our identity provider and your login page in a redirect loop and never actually completes. This started recently - it was working fine before.

We've tried clearing cookies, using a different browser, and having multiple team members attempt to log in, but everyone hits the same loop. There's no workaround on our end that we can find, so we're completely locked out of the platform right now.

This is a serious problem for us because we have an audit starting very soon and need access to pull evidence and update our compliance records. Every hour this stays broken puts that timeline at risk.

Can someone please look into this urgently and let us know what's going on? We need this fixed as soon as possible.

Thanks

subject: URGENT: Role change not taking effect - blocked from access I need
body:
Hi,

This is urgent - I need this fixed ASAP. We changed my role in the platform about 20 minutes ago (upgraded my permissions to give me access to a few sections I need to work in), but I'm still seeing the exact same restricted access as before the change. It's like the role update never applied.

I've tried refreshing the page and even closing the tab and reopening it, but nothing changes - I'm still locked out of the areas I should now have access to. I have work that's completely blocked because of this and I can't wait around for it to fix itself.

Can someone please look into this right away and tell me why the role change isn't taking effect? This is holding up time-sensitive work on my end.

Thanks,
[frustrated and stuck until this is resolved]

subject: URGENT: Need time-limited Contributor access (auto-expire after 30 days)
body:
Hi,

I need to grant a contractor Contributor access to our workspace, but I need it to automatically expire after 30 days without me having to remember to go in and remove it manually.

Is there a setting or option somewhere to set an expiration date on a role assignment? I've looked through the user/role management screens and can't find anything like that - just the option to assign the role, with no time limit attached.

This is urgent - I need to get this person access today, but I can't have their permissions sitting active indefinitely once their contract ends. Can someone tell me how to do this ASAP, or let me know if there's a fast turnaround fix coming? I'm blocked until I have a way to handle this.

Thanks,

subject: Ability to scope Viewer role to a single framework
body:
Hi,

Our external auditor needs read access to our account so they can review evidence, but we only want them to see the ISO 27001 framework, not everything else we have in the platform (SOC 2, other internal policies, etc).

When I try to set them up as a Viewer, it looks like that role gives access to the entire account rather than letting me limit it to just the one framework they're auditing. Is there a way to restrict Viewer access to a single framework? I don't see an option for this anywhere in the role/permissions settings.

This is holding things up on our end - the audit is starting very soon and we need to get the auditor access set up correctly before then. Right now we're stuck because we don't want to give them visibility into frameworks that aren't part of their scope, but there's no other way for them to get in and review evidence.

Can you let us know if this is something that can be added, or if there's a setting I'm missing?

Thanks,

subject: URGENT: Need time-limited Contributor access - 30 day auto-expiration not working/available
body:
Hi,

I need to grant a contractor Contributor access to our workspace, but only for 30 days - after that their access needs to automatically expire. I cannot find any way to set an expiration date or time limit on a role assignment anywhere in the platform.

This is urgent - I need to give this person access today, but I am not willing to grant permanent Contributor rights just to have to remember to manually go back and revoke it later. That's exactly the kind of thing that gets forgotten and turns into a compliance issue down the road.

Is there a setting I'm missing, or is this just not supported? If it's not supported, this is a pretty serious gap for a compliance platform - the whole point is to enforce least-privilege access, and there's no way I should have to rely on a calendar reminder to pull someone's permissions.

Please advise ASAP, I'm blocked on onboarding this contractor until I can be sure their access won't just sit there indefinitely.

Thanks,
[Customer]

subject: Invoice charged for seats we no longer have active
body:
Hi,

I just reviewed our latest invoice and it's charging us for a seat count that doesn't match what we actually have right now. We removed a couple of users a few weeks ago and I would have expected the billed seat count to reflect that, but instead we're being charged as if they're still active.

This isn't a huge deal financially, but it's frustrating - I had to go back and manually cross-check our user list against the invoice to figure out why the numbers didn't line up, which took time I didn't really have. We also have an audit coming up down the line, so I'd like to understand how seat counts get calculated so I'm not scrambling to explain a mismatch later.

Can someone explain why the invoice isn't reflecting our current active user count? Is there a setting or timing issue causing this, or is this just how billing works here? I'd rather not have to manually verify this every cycle if there's a way to avoid it.

Thanks,
Frustrated but hoping for a quick explanation

subject: Charged for a framework we removed BEFORE the 14-day trial ended
body:
We removed a framework from our account before the 14-day trial period was up specifically so we wouldn't get billed for it, and we still got charged for it anyway.

This is really frustrating - the whole point of removing it in time was to avoid this exact charge. I double checked our timeline and the removal was done before the trial window closed, so this shouldn't have happened. Now I have to go explain to our finance team why we're being billed for something we cancelled in time, which makes us look like we don't know what we're doing internally.

I know I could probably work around this by manually tracking removal dates and following up with support every time instead of relying on the trial window to just work, but that's not really sustainable when we're trying to manage multiple frameworks.

We also have an audit coming up down the line and would like to get this billing issue sorted well before then so it's not hanging over us.

Can you please look into why this charge went through and get it reversed? Also would like to understand if this could happen again with other frameworks we remove near the end of a trial.

subject: Cannot reduce account to one framework - stuck at two minimum
body:
We recently dropped one of our compliance frameworks and now only need to maintain one (SOC 2). When I go into account/plan settings to remove the second framework, the system won't let me go below two frameworks total - it just keeps forcing us to keep two active no matter what I do.

Is this a hard limit on our account? If so, this seems like a bug because we should be able to scale down to what we actually need. We have an audit starting very soon and need our workspace to reflect only the framework that's actually in scope - having the extra framework sitting there active is causing confusion with our evidence collection and is holding up our prep.

There's no workaround I can find on my end, so we're stuck until this gets sorted. Can someone take a look and let me know how to get this fixed? Time is tight on our end.
